name: Overhook Extraction
description: Master Overhook Extraction from New York Top. Step-by-step arm extraction against rubber guard control. Success rates: Beginner 30%, Intermediate 50%, Advanced 65%.
overview:
Overhook Extraction is a critical defensive technique for escaping the New York position within 10th Planet's Rubber Guard system. When trapped in New York Top, your arm is locked in a deep overhook while your opponent's shin crosses your back, breaking your posture and compromising your base. The overhook extraction addresses the arm control component, freeing your trapped limb and opening pathways to posture recovery and guard passing.

The technique operates on the principle that the overhook, while strong, has a structural weakness: it requires constant tension and positioning from the bottom player. By systematically changing the angle of your trapped elbow and using rotational movement rather than linear pulling, you exploit the overhook's blind spots. The key insight is that pulling straight back reinforces the overhook, while corkscrewing your elbow downward and toward your hip creates an angle the overhook cannot maintain.

Strategically, overhook extraction should not be attempted in isolation. The sequence must address base and posture concerns simultaneously. Attempting extraction without stable base invites sweeps; attempting it without addressing posture allows the bottom player to transition to other attacks like triangles or omoplatas. When executed correctly within the proper sequence, overhook extraction serves as the gateway from defensive survival in New York to offensive guard passing opportunities.
key_principles: Never pull the trapped arm straight back - this reinforces the overhook and triggers counter-attacks
Corkscrew motion (elbow down and toward hip) exploits the overhook's structural blind spot
Base establishment must precede extraction attempts - wide knees prevent sweeps during the technique
Posture engagement during extraction prevents triangle transitions as the arm comes free
Grip fighting the opponent's shin-controlling hand creates space for the extraction motion
Speed is secondary to angle - correct elbow angle succeeds where explosive pulling fails
Immediate guard passing engagement after extraction prevents opponent from re-establishing control
setup_requirements: Wide base established with knees spread to prevent sweeps during extraction attempt
Free hand actively grip-fighting opponent's shin-controlling grip or framing on their hip
Core engaged and weight distributed to resist forward pressure from opponent
Mental recognition that overhook grip has weakened or opponent's attention is divided

execution_steps.description: Widen your knees significantly to create a stable triangular base. Your free hand should frame on opponent's hip or grip-fight their shin-controlling hand. Without stable base, the extraction will result in a sweep.

Begin driving your chest upward while keeping your trapped elbow tight to your body. Do not attempt to stand or create distance yet - focus on engaging your posterior chain to resist the downward pull of the shin control.

Rotate your trapped elbow downward so it points toward your own hip rather than toward the floor. This subtle angle change is critical - it positions your arm for extraction rather than reinforcing the overhook's grip.

While maintaining the downward elbow angle, begin a spiraling motion toward your hip. Think of unscrewing a tight lid rather than pulling straight back. Your elbow leads the motion, your shoulder follows, and the arm extracts in a curved path.

As your arm begins to free, immediately drive your posture upward. The moment of extraction is when triangle attacks become available - keeping your head and shoulder high prevents the leg from shooting over your shoulder.

The instant your arm is free, establish control on opponent's legs or hips for guard passing. Do not pause to celebrate the extraction - your opponent will immediately attempt to re-establish New York or transition to other guards.

common_counters.counter: Opponent deepens overhook and tightens shoulder-to-armpit pressure when they feel extraction beginning
common_counters.your_response: Pause the extraction and focus on grip-fighting their shin control instead. Once shin control is compromised, return to the extraction sequence.

common_counters.counter: Opponent shoots leg over your shoulder for triangle as your arm extracts
common_counters.your_response: Drive posture up and stack immediately. The triangle attempt requires your head down - keeping posture defeats the counter and may create passing opportunities.

common_counters.counter: Opponent uses your extraction motion to generate hip bump sweep momentum
common_counters.your_response: Maintain wide base throughout and keep weight centered over both knees. If sweep begins, post with free hand and drive weight toward the sweep direction to counter.

common_counters.counter: Opponent transitions to Invisible Collar or Zombie before extraction completes
common_counters.your_response: Recognize early and shift to stack defense rather than continuing extraction. Address the new position before returning to overhook extraction attempts.

common_errors.error: Pulling trapped arm straight backward in a linear motion
common_errors.consequence: Reinforces the overhook's grip strength and may trigger immediate sweep or submission counter
common_errors.correction: Use corkscrew motion with elbow angled downward toward your hip - spiral out rather than pull back

common_errors.error: Attempting extraction before establishing wide base with knees spread
common_errors.consequence: Opponent sweeps during the extraction attempt when your focus is on arm rather than balance
common_errors.correction: Always widen base first, creating stable platform that can absorb sweep attempts during extraction

common_errors.error: Relaxing posture engagement during the extraction motion
common_errors.consequence: Creates opening for triangle attack as arm extracts with head remaining low and vulnerable
common_errors.correction: Drive chest and head upward throughout extraction - posture and extraction happen together, not sequentially

common_errors.error: Pausing after successful extraction instead of immediately engaging guard pass
common_errors.consequence: Opponent re-establishes New York control or transitions to alternative guard before you capitalize
common_errors.correction: Treat extraction as the beginning of your attack sequence, not the end - immediately control legs for passing

common_errors.error: Flaring elbow outward during extraction attempt
common_errors.consequence: Creates perfect angle for armbar attack and may hyperextend elbow against overhook pressure
common_errors.correction: Keep elbow tight to body throughout, pointing downward toward hip rather than outward to the side

training_progressions.description: Practice the elbow angle and spiral motion in isolation without partner resistance. Partner holds static overhook while you drill the correct extraction path 50+ repetitions per session until the motion becomes automatic.

Combine extraction mechanics with base widening and posture engagement. Partner adds light resistance to test your structure. Focus on maintaining wide knees and upward posture throughout the extraction sequence.

Partner actively attempts triangle, sweeps, and position transitions during your extraction. Develop ability to recognize counters early and adjust your response. Practice abandoning extraction to address new threats when necessary.

Execute complete sequence from New York escape through guard pass in live rolling. Track success rate and identify which counters give you trouble. Refine timing and develop personal variations based on your body type and game.

variants_and_adaptations.description: Rather than isolating arm movement, use explosive hip drive backward while maintaining elbow angle. Your body weight assists the extraction. Higher risk of sweep but faster execution when timing is correct.
variants_and_adaptations.when_to_use: When opponent's shin control has momentarily weakened and you sense opportunity for rapid escape

variants_and_adaptations.description: Instead of corkscrewing out, swim your trapped arm forward and around opponent's head, transitioning to a cross-face position. This reverses the direction and can surprise opponents expecting backward extraction.
variants_and_adaptations.when_to_use: When opponent is defending conventional extraction by deepening their overhook aggressively

knowledge_assessment.question: What is the primary goal of Overhook Extraction?
knowledge_assessment.answer: The primary goal is to free your trapped arm from the opponent's deep overhook control in New York position, creating the opportunity to recover posture and begin guard passing. The extraction is not the end goal but rather the gateway that enables offensive action from what was a compromised defensive position.

knowledge_assessment.question: Why does pulling straight backward fail against a properly set overhook?
knowledge_assessment.answer: Pulling straight back reinforces the overhook's biomechanical advantage. The overhook is designed to resist linear pulling force - the opponent's shoulder-to-armpit pressure creates a wedge that tightens under direct resistance. The solution is angular extraction using a corkscrew motion that exploits the overhook's blind spot below and behind the grip.

knowledge_assessment.question: What position must you establish before attempting overhook extraction and why?
knowledge_assessment.answer: You must establish a wide base with knees spread before attempting extraction. Without stable base, the focus required for extraction leaves you vulnerable to sweeps - the bottom player can use hip bump or other sweep mechanics while your attention is on the arm. Wide base creates a stable platform that can absorb sweep attempts during the extraction sequence.

knowledge_assessment.question: Your opponent shoots their leg over your shoulder as your arm extracts - what went wrong and how do you respond?
knowledge_assessment.answer: Your posture dropped during the extraction, creating the opening for triangle. The response is immediate stacking - drive your head and shoulder up and forward while pushing into your opponent's hips. This removes the space needed for the triangle to lock. The correction for future attempts is maintaining upward posture throughout extraction, not just at the end.

knowledge_assessment.question: What should you do the instant your arm successfully extracts from the overhook?
knowledge_assessment.answer: Immediately establish grips for guard passing - control the opponent's legs or hips before they can re-establish New York or transition to alternative guards. The extraction window is brief; pausing to reset allows the opponent to recover their offensive structure. Treat extraction as the beginning of your attack, not the conclusion of your defense.

knowledge_assessment.question: Describe the correct elbow angle and motion path for the corkscrew extraction technique?
knowledge_assessment.answer: The elbow should angle downward toward your own hip rather than pointing at the floor or flaring outward. From this angle, execute a spiraling motion as if unscrewing a tight lid - the elbow leads, drawing a curved path toward your hip while the shoulder follows. This spiral exploits the overhook's structural weakness at angles below and behind the grip line.

knowledge_assessment.question: Your opponent deepens their overhook when they feel your extraction beginning - how do you adapt?
knowledge_assessment.answer: Pause the extraction attempt and redirect your effort to grip-fighting their shin-controlling hand instead. The shin control and overhook work together as a system - compromising the shin control reduces the structural integrity of the entire New York position. Once their shin control weakens, return to the overhook extraction with improved odds of success.

knowledge_assessment.question: When should you abandon an overhook extraction attempt and address a different threat?
knowledge_assessment.answer: Abandon extraction immediately when you recognize opponent transitioning to Invisible Collar, Zombie, triangle, or other advanced attacks. These transitions change the threat profile and require different defensive responses. Continuing extraction while a new attack develops wastes the defensive window. Address the immediate threat first, then return to extraction when you've stabilized.

safety_considerations: Overhook extraction carries moderate injury risk primarily to the shoulder and elbow of the trapped arm. Never explosively yank your arm to escape - this can hyperextend the elbow against the overhook pressure or strain the shoulder capsule. The corkscrew motion should be smooth and controlled. If you feel significant pain during extraction, stop and work to create space rather than forcing through. Partners should release immediately if the person on top signals discomfort. When drilling, start with zero resistance and progress slowly to ensure both partners understand the mechanics before adding intensity.
position_integration: Overhook Extraction is the central technique in the New York Top escape sequence, serving as the bridge between defensive survival and offensive opportunity. Within the broader rubber guard defense system, it works in conjunction with base widening and posture recovery - these three techniques form an integrated escape methodology. Successfully extracting the overhook opens direct pathways to pressure passing, leg drag, or toreando-style passes. The technique also teaches principles applicable to overhook escapes in other contexts including guillotine defense and front headlock escapes where similar arm-trapping mechanics apply.
